events.text_en: A woodcutter's boy of Tiều Ca Trấn carries a load of wood up to Không Sơn Viện and does not come down; the academy sets him to sweeping.
On the night Thôi Bất Kiến dies, his student reads aloud in the empty academy until dawn, and promises that the mountain will keep its voices.
The year Thúy Vi seals the stone gate on the ridge, the abbey's reader finds another way in, through the haze.
Mâu Hành Đáo, prior of Vân Khởi Quán, comes down to dig at Vân Gian Trấn and is taken by the second slide.
Vân Khởi Quán's prior says the abbey will take any child Thúy Vi's gate turns away, if they can sit until dusk.
The abbot gives the bell of the empty hall to a mica-miner's daughter.
